meta.method_note: NHF = neural horizon field (pipeline/nhf_model.py): a coarse ray cast from 2,448 LOLA samples per point (72 azimuths x 34 distances, 50 m - 300 km) corrected by a neural network trained on 100,000 precise horizons; precise = ray casting with pipeline/terrain.py (about 3 million samples per point)
meta.az_convention: from each point's own local north (along its meridian toward the equator) toward east; index k = azimuth k*1 deg
meta.elevation: deg above the observer's local horizontal plane (normal to the sphere radius), lunar curvature included

terrain.source: NASA LRO LOLA GDR polar DEMs (PDS, imbrium.mit.edu)
terrain.horizon_method: max terrain elevation angle along great circles, exact 3-D sphere geometry (curvature included); 40 m steps to 20 km, 80 m steps beyond, up to 320 km; 40 m DEM where it exists; rays stop where the DEMs end

meta.sun_earth_note: Sun/Earth az/el in panorama_im2.json are for the grid centre G0158. For the other points, re-project the Sun/Earth direction vectors into each point's own local frame (as in the approach-path code of pipeline/make_inputs.py): across this grid the horizontal plane tilts by up to 0.026 deg and local north turns by up to 0.29 deg.
meta.si_use: Code written with Claude Code (AI) during the event; terrain is NASA LOLA.

nhf.inputs: position (x, y) + elevation angles of the LOLA terrain at 72 grid azimuths x 34 distances (50 m - 300 km) seen from ground + 0 m and + 2 m
nhf.outputs: horizon at 720 grid azimuths for 0 m and 2 m, as a correction to the coarse horizon (highest feature angle per direction)

training_data.region: -84.5 deg to the pole, uniform in area
training_data.held_out: within 2.0 km of the 150 validation points and of the IM-2 grid centre
